title: How the nephron makes urine
sub: Follow one parcel of filtrate: each segment's wall decides whether water or salt may leave, and the depth of the medulla decides how far it goes.

phases.name: Glomerular filtration
phases.shows: Plasma is filtered from the glomerular capillaries into Bowman's space by a net filtration pressure of 10 mmHg (55 − 15 − 30); the parcel starts as 300 mOsm/kg filtrate.

phases.name: Proximal convoluted tubule
phases.shows: Iso-osmotic reabsorption: Na⁺ is pumped out and water follows, so ~65% of the volume leaves while osmolality stays 300; all glucose and most bicarbonate are reclaimed.

phases.name: Thin descending limb
phases.shows: Water-only wall: water leaves into the increasingly salty medulla, so the fluid concentrates to ~1200 mOsm/kg at the loop tip.

phases.name: Thick ascending limb
phases.shows: Water-tight wall: NKCC2 pumps NaCl out, so the fluid dilutes (to ~100) while the interstitium is kept salty; the single effect that builds the gradient.

phases.name: Distal convoluted tubule
phases.shows: NCC (thiazide-sensitive) removes more NaCl with no water; the fluid becomes most dilute; the macula densa sits at its start.

phases.name: Cortical collecting duct
phases.shows: Principal cells: aldosterone drives ENaC Na⁺ uptake and K⁺ secretion; with ADH, water leaves and the fluid returns to ~300.

phases.name: Medullary collecting duct
phases.shows: With ADH (AQP2), water leaves into the deep medulla so the urine concentrates toward ~1200 mOsm/kg, with under 1% of the filtrate left.

parts.name: Afferent arteriole
parts.shows: Afferent arteriole: brings blood into the glomerulus; its pressure sets glomerular capillary pressure.

parts.name: Glomerulus
parts.shows: Glomerular capillary tuft where plasma is filtered.

parts.name: Efferent arteriole
parts.shows: Efferent arteriole: carries blood out of the glomerulus into the peritubular capillaries and vasa recta.

parts.name: Bowman's capsule
parts.shows: Bowman's capsule: collects the filtrate; its pressure (15 mmHg) opposes filtration.

parts.name: Proximal convoluted tubule
parts.shows: Proximal convoluted tubule with brush border: bulk iso-osmotic reabsorption (Na⁺, water, glucose, HCO₃⁻).

parts.name: Thin descending limb
parts.shows: Thin descending limb: permeable to water (AQP1), not salt.

parts.name: Thick ascending limb
parts.shows: Thick ascending limb: NKCC2 salt pump, impermeable to water; target of loop diuretics.

parts.name: Macula densa
parts.shows: Macula densa: tall cells of the late thick limb that sense NaCl delivery next to the glomerulus (tubuloglomerular feedback).

parts.name: Distal convoluted tubule
parts.shows: Distal convoluted tubule: NCC salt uptake, water-tight; target of thiazides.

parts.name: Collecting duct
parts.shows: Collecting duct: aldosterone (ENaC, ROMK) and ADH-controlled water reabsorption (AQP2); sets final urine concentration.

parts.name: Peritubular capillaries
parts.shows: Peritubular capillaries: take back what the cortical tubule reabsorbs.

parts.name: Vasa recta
parts.shows: Vasa recta: hairpin capillaries in the medulla that supply it without washing out the gradient (countercurrent exchange).

parts.name: Medullary interstitium
parts.shows: Medullary interstitium: osmolality rising from 300 at the corticomedullary border to 1200 at the papilla.

readouts.label: Tubular fluid
readouts.shows: Osmolality of the tubular fluid in the parcel right now.

readouts.label: Filtrate left
readouts.shows: Percentage of the original filtrate volume still left in the tubule.

readouts.label: Interstitium here
readouts.shows: Osmolality of the interstitium around the parcel at its current depth.

readouts.label: Flow at this point
readouts.shows: Tubular flow at this point scaled to both kidneys, in litres per day.

readouts.label: Lumen minus interstitium
readouts.shows: Tubular fluid minus interstitial osmolality: negative means the fluid is more dilute than its surroundings.

readouts.label: Water leaving parcel
readouts.shows: Rate at which water is leaving the parcel.

readouts.label: Solute leaving parcel
readouts.shows: Rate at which solute is leaving the parcel.

readouts.label: Glucose left
readouts.shows: Percentage of filtered glucose still in the tubule.

readouts.label: Bicarbonate left
readouts.shows: Percentage of filtered bicarbonate still in the tubule.

readouts.label: Depth into medulla
readouts.shows: How deep the parcel is in the medulla (0 = corticomedullary border, 1 = papilla tip; negative = cortex).

readouts.label: Net filtration pressure
readouts.shows: Net filtration pressure across the glomerular membrane.

readouts.label: Glomerular capillary pressure
readouts.shows: Hydrostatic pressure in the glomerular capillaries, pushing fluid out.

readouts.label: Bowman's space pressure
readouts.shows: Hydrostatic pressure in Bowman's space, pushing back.

readouts.label: Plasma oncotic pressure
readouts.shows: Plasma oncotic pressure (proteins in the capillary), pulling fluid back.

concepts: sites of action of diuretics (loop, thiazide)
not_shown: afferent or efferent arteriole constriction (the plate keeps both arterioles fixed)

lenses.title: The filtration barrier
lenses.shows: The three layers between blood and Bowman's space (fenestrated endothelium, negatively charged basement membrane, podocyte slit diaphragms), water and small solutes crossing while albumin and red cells are held back, and the Starling pressures that add up to the net filtration pressure.
concepts: Starling forces and net filtration pressure

lenses.title: Inside a proximal tubule cell
lenses.shows: SGLT2, NHE3 and aquaporin-1 on the brush border and the Na⁺/K⁺ pump, GLUT2 and NBCe1 on the blood side: Na⁺ is pumped out, water follows, and glucose and bicarbonate are reclaimed while the fluid stays at 300 mOsm/kg.

lenses.title: The countercurrent multiplier
lenses.shows: The loop of Henle as a hairpin against the medullary gradient: water leaves the thin descending limb so the fluid concentrates toward 1200, NaCl is pumped out of the water-tight thick ascending limb so the fluid dilutes, with the parcel's own values at each depth.
concepts: different permeabilities of the two limbs

lenses.title: Inside a thick ascending limb cell
lenses.shows: NKCC2 taking up Na⁺, K⁺ and 2Cl⁻, K⁺ recycling through ROMK that makes the lumen positive and drives Mg²⁺ and Ca²⁺ between cells, and the water-tight wall, so salt leaves without water; loop diuretics block NKCC2.

lenses.title: A principal cell and ADH
lenses.shows: ADH binding V2 receptors, cAMP moving aquaporin-2 into the apical membrane so water leaves toward the salty interstitium; aldosterone driving ENaC Na⁺ uptake and ROMK K⁺ secretion.

lenses.title: Where the filtrate goes
lenses.shows: The share of the 180 L/day of filtrate still in the tubule after each segment, how much water each segment removes and the osmolality leaving it, ending at the final urine volume and concentration.
